FLOOR FINISH /WAX

Finish/Wax - A chemical applied on the floor after applying the sealer 

                    Kinds of Waxes:



 Emulsion Wax - is water-based wax (liquid wax and slip resistance wax)  
      
Two Kinds of Emulsion Wax:


a. Buffable Wax – It is a wax applied on the floor and after drying needs polishing.
Example: Sunshine Wax or Traffic Grade Wax, Routine






 Non-Buffable Wax – It is a wax applied on the floor and after drying does not need  polishing.
Example: Hyper 25, 18 plus and Complete wax, Stride wax, Grand Entrance

Solvent Wax - is a kerosene or petroleum-based wax.


Two Kinds of Solvent Wax:


    Paste - for household use. Example: Star paste wax,













Liquid - for industrial or commercial use, warehouse (Bodega), School floors.  Example: Prime Gloss, Premium Gloss, and Traffic Wax

3. Sealer Wax - chemical applied on the floor to seal the pores, edges and grouting of the floor  after stripping
Example: Premium Shield, Over and Under, First Base.


















Spray Buff Concentrate - chemical we use in spray buffing the floor. It is usually done after 3 days after  the application of floor finish wax.
Example: Premium shield, Snap Back, Low & Behold.

*Note: Always read label for the Description and Direction of Chemicals.

HC   = Heavy Cleaning 
 MC  = Mild Cleaning  
LC   = Light Cleaning
RTU  = Ready To Use

 example: (chemicals) – 10ml : 30l – (water)

Ang pressure washer ay isang makina na gumagamit ng mataas na presyon ng tubig upang linisin ang iba't ibang uri ng dumi, putik, amag, pintura, at iba pang nakadikit na mga bagay sa mga ibabaw tulad ng sasakyan, sahig, pader, at konkretong daan.

Mga Gamit ng Pressure Washer
✔️ Paglilinis ng sasakyan, motorsiklo, at bisikleta✔️ Pagtanggal ng lumot at amag sa dingding o sahig✔️ Pag-aalis ng natuyong putik sa driveway o kalsada✔️ Pagtanggal ng lumang pintura bago mag-repaint✔️ Paglilinis ng bubong at kanal (gutter)
1. SURIIN ANG KUNDISYON NG MAKINA AT ACCESSORIES
2. IKABIT NG MAAYOS ANG PRESSURE WASHER HOSE AT ACCESSORIES AT GUN
3.IKUNUKTA ANG SUCTION AT SPRAY HOSEAT TIYAKIN SAPAT ANG SUPPLY NA TUBIG.
4. ION ANG MAKINA SA PAMAMAGITAN NG PAGPINDUT SA POWER BUTTON
5. GAMITIN ANG PRESSURE WASHER, ITUTOK ITO DALAWA HANGANG TATLONG TALAMPAKAN MULA SA IBABAW
6. HUWAG ITUTOK ANG PRESSURE WASHER SA TAO, HAYOP OR SA DIKURYENTENG KAGAMITAN.

Ang floor polisher ay isang makina na ginagamit upang linisin, pakinisin, at bigyan ng kinang ang sahig. Ito ay may umiikot na pad o brush na tumutulong sa pagtanggal ng dumi, gasgas, at lumang wax sa sahig.

Gamit ng Floor Polisher

✅ Paglilinis ng sahig – Inaalis ang dumi, alikabok, at mantsa.✅ Pagpapakintab ng sahig – Ginagamit kasama ng floor wax upang           magbigay ng makintab na finish.✅ Pagtanggal ng lumang wax – Tumutulong sa pag-rewax ng sahig.✅ Pang-maintenance ng sahig – Pinipigilan ang mabilis na pagkasira ng sahig sa pamamagitan ng regular na polishing.

MGA HAKBANG SA PAG GAMIT NG FLOOR POLISHER

1. Suriin ang kondisyon ng Polisher, mga piyesa at kumpletong accessories 
2. I-set up ang polisher sa pamamagitan ng pagtanggal ng electrical cord mula sa cord holder. 
3. I-set up ang polisher pad sa gitna ng pad holder at ipasok ito sa gear lock       ng motor. 
4. I-unlock ang butterfly lock para sa nais na taas na angkop sa posisyon ng iyong mga kamay. 
5. Isaksak ang saksakan ng kuryente at pindutin ang switch ng hawakan upang simulan ang polisher upang tumakbo. 
6. Habang nagsisimulang paikutin ng Polisher ang pad, hawakan ang iyong posisyon upang kontrolin ang polisher. 
7. Upang lumipat sa kanan, hawakan ang hawakan at dahan-dahang pindutin pababa. Dahan-dahang hilahin ang hawakan pataas upang lumipat sa kaliwang bahagi. 
8. Bumalik upang sa susunod na bahagi ng sahig para puliduhin. Ulitin ang parehong posisyon upang mapolish ang buong sahig.

Ang vacuum cleaner ay isang makina na ginagamit upang sumipsip ng alikabok, dumi, buhok, at maliliit na debris mula sa sahig, carpet, kasangkapan, at iba pang mga ibabaw. Gumagamit ito ng motor na lumilikha ng suction upang hilahin ang dumi papasok sa isang filter o bag.

Gamit ng Vacuum Cleaner

✅ Paglilinis ng sahig at carpet – Epektibong nag-aalis ng dumi, alikabok, at buhok ng alagang hayop.✅ Pagtanggal ng alikabok sa muwebles at tela – Puwedeng gamitin sa sofa, kurtina, at kama.✅ Panglinis ng sasakyan – Tinatanggal ang dumi at alikabok sa loob ng kotse.✅ Pag-aalis ng allergens at bacteria – Tumutulong sa mas malinis at ligtas na hangin sa paligid

MGA HAKBANG SA PAG GAMIT NG VACUUM

Suriin ang tumatakbong kondisyon ng Vacuum cleaner at mga accessories nito.
Magtipon ng mga accessory tulad ng vacuum hose, suction tube, at vacuum head, pagkatapos ay suriin ang filter bag sa loob ng vacuum casing.
Pindutin ang berdeng button para i-on ang vacuum cleaner
Hawakan ang Suction Tube at simulan ang pag-vacuum sa sahig ng karpet
Gumawa ng push and pull motion para masipsip ang lahat ng lupa at dumi sa carpet floor
Para sa mahirap abutin at masikip na sulok, gamitin ang naaangkop na nozzle na angkop sa laki ng mga lugar na hindi maabot.
Pindutin ang pulang button para patayin ang vacuum cleaner at tiyaking i-unplug ang cord.
Alisin ang lahat ng mga accessory at punasan upang alisin ang alikabok.Itapon ang alikabok/dumi sa loob ng casing.Linisin ang filter bag. 
Hugasan kung kinakailangan at patuyuin ng maayos

OPERATING PROCEDURE ESCALATOR CLEANER

 BRUSHING

Check the running condition of Escalator Machine and its accessories.
Position the Machine at the foot of the escalator.
Place the Machine on the first step making sure that the stabilizing  wheels are in channels.
Start the Machine by lowering the handle. Start the escalator
Keep a good grip on the machine by firmly gripping the handle and  let it complete at least three full rotations of the stairs.
Stop the machine by raising the handle.
Move the Machine to the other side of the step and do the same
BRUSHING procedure.

 WASHING

Check the running condition of Escalator Machine and its accessories.
Prepare the detergent solution using the specific product for cleaning  escalators.
Fill up the tanks with the special detergent solution provided.
Place the machine on the first step and make sure that the stabilizing wheels are inserted into the channel,  otherwise the machine could work irregularly. Start the machine by lowering the handle.
Dispense the detergent solution by moving the appropriate lever found under the handle and allow it to  complete as many rotations as necessary on the stairs until all the dirt is removed.
From time to time, empty the recovery tank to prevent it from overfilling.
Stop Machine by raising the handle.
Move the Machine to the other side of the step and do the same WASHING procedure.

Dry Foam Carpet Shampoo- chemical used in dry foam carpet shampooing.  Example: Power Foam/Campaign TPM, Rug bee Regular Shampoo, Revitalize301  Dilution: 1:10(HC), 1:20(MC), 1:30(LC)

.

1. Move all of the furniture. Anytime you shampoo your carpets, move all of the furniture completely out of the room, if possible. If you can’t move it out of the room, move it all to one side of the room. At the very least, move any small pieces of furniture and remove any other clutter from the room.

If you have large pieces of furniture that are difficult to move, it’s your decision to leave them in the room. If you leave furniture in the room, it will be harder to shampoo because you have to work around it.

If you can’t or don’t want to move large furniture, you can place squares of aluminum foil, wood blocks, or plastic film under the legs or base to protect them from water during shampooing

2. Vacuum the room thoroughly. Carpet shampooers have a vacuuming feature, but they are meant to suck up water and small dirt particles. Vacuuming the room will remove larger dirt, hair, and dust balls, leaving the carpet ready for shampoo. It will also fluff the carpet up, which makes shampooing more effective.

Since you are going to the extra effort of shampooing, vacuum a little more than you usually would. Go in straight lines up and down the room and then do another set that crisscrosses the first set.

As you vacuum, look for stains that need pre-treatment before shampooing. Set a sticky note or marker of some kind on the spot so you can easily find it.

3. Treat specific stain that you find. With a basic carpet stain remover, spray any stains and let the cleaner work as directed. If it says to blot it up with a wet towel, do so. If it says to leave it and let the shampooer pick it up, do so. Some stains may require something besides stain remover.

Some carpet shampoos are meant for tough stains, so you may not need to use a stain remover.

4. Make sure you know how the machine works. If the shampooer is new or you are renting it, read the instructions for use. If there are no instructions, at least examine the machine to see the various parts, buttons, and settings. There are many kinds of carpet cleaners and they work in various ways. It is important to know how yours works.

Some shampooers work if you push them forward like a vacuum, but many others require that you walk backwards and pull the shampooer along with you. If you try to use the shampooer in a way besides how it was designed, your carpet won’t get clean.

Look up tutorials online to learn the most effective way to use the specific shampooer you have.

Before you rent or purchase a machine, do some research to find out if it's been verified by the Carpet and Rug Institute (CRI), which ensures the machine works well and effectively cleans carpets. It's important to use a machine that works well since you likely won't clean your carpet often.

5. Fill the machine with the directed amount of water. Some shampooers have a removable clean water tank and others have a fixed water tank. Pay attention to the max fill line and do not add more water than it says. The line is there to make sure the machine runs properly.

Follow any instructions regarding hot or cold water. Hot water activates soap better, so it is usually best.

6. Add the carpet soap. Choose a soap that is designed to work with the shampooer that you have because not every soap will work with every machine. Pour only the amount of soap that is directed, as using more can clog the machine or leave soap scum on your carpet. Pay attention to whether the soap is added to the clean water or into a separate compartment on the shampooer.

Read reviews online of the best carpet shampoos and consult the instructions on the shampooer to determine if there is a specific soap that works best.

Most shampooers will work without soap and will still clean the carpets to an extent, so it is better to put less than enough soap than too much

7. Start in a corner and make strips. Choose a corner of the room to start in, getting the shampooer as close to the walls as possible. Walk from that corner to the wall on the other side of the room. Then turn around, move the shampooer to a new line that slightly overlaps the first, and walk back towards the wall you started at. Repeat this process across the entire room.

Shampooers are not meant to be pulled back and forth in a random pattern like vacuums are. Making straight lines across the room is the most effective cleaning method

8. Pull the machine slowly. Shampooers take more time to work than vacuums. They have to shoot soapy water down into the carpet and immediately suck it back up. If you pull the shampooer too fast, it will not suck all of the dirty water up, leaving your carpets wet and still dirty. Be patient and pull the shampooer at a rate of one step per second, give or take.

It may feel like you are going too slow and that it is taking too long, but the slower you go, the deeper the machine can clean your carpet

9. Pay attention to the motor sound. Most shampooers have a float valve in the dirty water tank to warn you once the tank is full. The motor will distinctly change sounds when the float valve engages. Stop immediately when the tank is full or you could damage the machine. The machine might have a visible light or gauge that shows you that the dirty water tank is full.

You can also watch the machine and notice the water level of the clean and dirty tanks. If you notice you are almost out of clean water, go ahead and stop.

You may need to empty the dirty water and refill the clean water multiple times before you are finished shampooing the room. It depends on the room size, the tank sizes, and exactly how slowly you are moving. If your carpet is very dirty or worn, you might run the shampooer over the carpet more than once, which will require that you empty and refill the water tank multiple times.

10. Empty dirty water into the toilet or outside. Shampooers pull up dirt and debris that can clog sink and shower drains. The toilet has a larger pipe and can handle this material, but dumping the water outside is usually the best option when available.

If you have to dump dirty water down the sink or shower drain, dump it slowly with hot water running the entire time. This will help keep the drain from clogging.

11. Run the shampooer a second time with cold water and no soap. While the shampooer is designed to suck up all of the soap and dirty water, it will sometimes leave more behind than you want it to. A second pass over the entire room will get any soap residue and remaining dirt. You can go a little quicker on the second pass than you did while you were shampooing.

The emphasis is on cold water because hot water will activate the soap that remains which could cause it to suds up again.

On this time around, take off your shoes and socks so that you don’t leave any dirt on the freshly cleaned carpet

12. Allow the carpet to dry completely before putting furniture back in the room. It can take six or more hours for the carpet to fully dry, depending on the carpet thickness and room size. Your shampooer may have instructions about drying time. Turn on an overhead fan or place fans and blowers at intervals around the room to decrease drying time.

If you put furniture back on wet carpet, it can cause bad indentations, and mildew can build up because the wet carpet has no airflow on it.

You may want to hang a sign saying that you have just shampooed the carpet so that people will not walk around on the wet carpet

13. Rinse and empty both tanks of the machine after each use. After your final pass, dump any remaining water out of both water tanks. Rinse the dirty water tank out thoroughly so that no grime remains in it. Emptying the tanks all the way keeps mildew from growing and keeps the machine in top working order.

If the tank has a cap of any kind, leave it off for a day or two to allow the excess water to completely evaporate

PREVENTIVE MAINTENANCE:

Spray Buffing - is the spraying of a mixture of water with spray buff concentrate or water with wax  on the floor surface while damp polish it until dry and shiny. To remove / repair surface  imperfections. This is done weekly, biweekly or every other day, or as required by traffic level.

Materials and Supplies: Dust mop, soft broom, dustpan, clean red pad, mop bucket and wringer,  wet mop, spray gun, spray buffing chemical, low speed polisher (175-400 rpm)

Steps/Procedures:

 Ipunin ang lahat ng mga materyales at kagamitan. Walisin ang sahig simula sa pinakamalayong sulok ng silid o dust mop para sa mas malalaking bukas na lugar tulad ng mga pasilyo at lobby.  
 Ilagay ang Wet Floor sign, dilute ang spray buff concentrate sa spray gun.  
 Dust mop at damp mop sa sahig para maalis ang mga spot sa sahig.  
 Ilagay ang Polisher sa posisyon at mag-spray ng kaunting kemikal sa sahig sa unahan ng floor machine.  
5. Pahiran ang sahig gamit ang pulang pad at ikalat ang solusyon sa sahig. Ipagpatuloy ang buffing hanggang ang ibabaw ay ganap na tuyo at makintab.  
6. Huwag hayaang mag-load ang pulang pad. Baliktarin ang mga ito o palitan nang madalas.  
7. Dust mop o walisin ang sahig na nagreresulta sa buffing operation.  
8. Alisin ang Wet Floor sign, linisin ang lahat ng materyales at kagamitan bago itago

SAFEKEEPING OF EQUIPMENT,  CLEANING MATERIALS AND SUPPLIES
Guidelines and Reminders:
Equipment must be kept in the proper storage areas after using. Make sure the equipment and  materials are cleaned by the end user, so that the next user will do the same. (1st Shift to 2nd Shift)

Check and place all equipment accessories in the designated storage place. Doing this will be easier  for the users to get the needed items when it is always stored properly.
(Polisher Brush, Pad Holder, Nylon Brush, Vacuum Hose, Handle, Nozzle etc.)

Cleaning Materials must be also stored in proper places. Wash them first before storing to prevent  unpleasant smells. To prevent deformation, hang them in a cool dry place to make them last longer.  (Mop, Soft Broom, Dust pan, Stick Broom, Push Brush, Hand brush, Dust mop, etc.)

Cleaning Supplies and Chemicals must have their own safekeeping place or cabinets. Use labels  such as:
Waxes, Wax stripper, Crystallizer and Spray Buff Chemical
Toilet Bowl Cleaner and Disinfectant
Air Freshener, Deodorizer and Neutralizer

Janitorial Cart, Utility Cart, Trash Dollies, Wet Floor Sign and door mat must be clean before storing.

Make or submit monthly inventory and checking of Equipment for its running condition.

Put a Caution sign or warning information on a defective equipment so that the next shift will not  use it to avoid accidents. Endorsement of both shifts is required before the end of each shift.

Wash mops after use and hang them with the yarn facing away from the wall. Do the same with  dust mops.

Wash and hang Polisher Pads (Stripping, Scrubbing, Buffing and Polishing). These pads have their  own cleaning and shining chemical content, based on color and cleaning contents.

SAFETY RULES IN DOING HOUSEKEEPING WORKS

Maintain clean, hygienic and attractive surroundings without disrupting other people. Cleaning  methods should not affect or harm the environment as well.

Wear complete uniform, proper Identification card, working shoes (black), clean haircut, No  mustache and beard.

Prepare all the materials and equipment that will be used on the given task. Check all items if they  are complete and equipment are in good condition. We should not consume time looking for other  cleaning materials. Know where all the equipment and materials are stored.

Place CAUTION SIGN, CAUTION TAPE and WET FLOOR SIGN on the areas that will be cleaned.

For Hospital cleaning:
Operating Room – Wear protective clothing, surgical cap, mask, gown, shoes and gloves.
Isolation Room – Read Isolation Card to determine the protective clothing to be worn. Put  on gown, mask, and overshoe boots.
Follow the safety standard cleaning procedure in cleaning the Isolation Room.
Ask permission to the Shift Supervisor / Nurses Station before cleaning Room.

For Swimming Pool Cleaning:
Pool Maintenance – Wearing proper uniform during daily pool maintenance.
Pool Treatment – Use test kit for water testing before chemical application. Wear hand  gloves and mask.

Interior wall & ceiling cleaning: for high wall cleaning, use ladder, can be used scaffolding for  high ceiling, safety belt is required to be worn.

For Carpet Cleaning, Test first the chemicals (Shampoo & Spotter) in an inconspicuous area to  prevent damage on the carpet. Same as upholstered chair cleaning.

While cleaning, DO NOT PLACE all your cleaning materials and equipment everywhere that may  obstruct in the area, Instead Place them in a corner which you think is safe and away from  damages.

Always wash your hands and arms before and after the cleaning task is performed.
